SPN 3226 FMI 4.issue: Aftertreatment outlet NOx sensor circuit low

WP3392519.name: Dryer thermal fuse (196°F)
WP3392519.safetyNote: Unplug the dryer before touching anything. If it's a gas dryer, stop and call a pro.
WP3392519.rootCauseNote: A blown thermal fuse almost always means the vent is clogged. Clean the lint trap duct and the outside vent, or the new fuse will blow too, and it's a fire risk.
installSteps: Unplug the dryer from the wall and pull it out so you can reach the back.
Disconnect the vent hose from the back of the dryer and set it aside.
Remove the screws along the bottom edge of the back panel, then lift the panel off.
Find the thermal fuse: a small white oval piece with two wires, mounted on the exhaust duct near the blower.
Pull the two wires off the old fuse and remove its one screw.
Mount the new fuse with the same screw and push the two wires back on, either way round.
Clean the lint out of the vent hose and the duct, put the panel back, reconnect the vent, plug in, and run it on high for a minute.
